description: Return common measured facts with stable metric semantics. Use gpu_devices or activity_summary to separate visible GPUs from GPUs with activity. Use activity_summary for per-report category coverage and active GPU attribution. Use kernel_summary for launch counts, unique kernel names, total time, mean time, and longest single launch; use --metric max_single_duration for the longest launch. Use an unqualified cuda_api_summary for ambiguous API timing so total, mean, and longest-event interpretations stay visible. Use nvtx_presence for the exact NVTX_EVENTS row count. Use memcpy_summary with metric total_bytes for largest memory operation by byte volume. Use timeline_summary for bounded kernel timeline coverage and idle-gap facts. Use frame_summary to locate a graphics frame's time window and per-frame CPU frame time (DXGI/Vulkan/OpenGL present rows, else DxgKrnl ETW Present); stutter is one use, but per-frame timing answers any frame-time question. Use frame_scan --frame <N> to scan a frame's window for ETW and WDDM event evidence against a baseline neighbor frame; it returns event counts (not a cause verdict). Use graphics_api_summary for per-API DX12/Vulkan/OpenGL call timing (count, total/avg/max ms) ranked by total time; add --frame <N> to scope to a frame window (no nanosecond pasting) with each API's pct_of_frame, plus the paired GPU workload table. Use graphics_api_distribution for session-wide per-API call-duration percentiles (min/median/p95/p99/max) to separate steady-state cost from the tail; --metric <api_name> narrows to one API. Use graphics_api_timeline --metric <api_name> to detect back-to-back serialized chaining of one API's calls (the in-order command-queue pattern behind tiled-resource stutter). Use thread_scheduling for per-thread on-CPU and blocked-time upper bounds, with `*_confirmed_pct` as confidence in each bound: near 100% means confirmed sched-in/sched-out pairs, while a low value means missing transitions inflated the upper bound. It also reports the dominant block reason (the fence-wait / lock-contention / preemption distinction) and top OSRT_API blocking waits (e.g. `WaitForSingleObjectEx` on Windows, `pthread_cond_wait` on Linux); add --frame <N> to scope to one frame window. Use callstack_summary for leaf-symbol hotspots (cpuCycles=1 periodic samples = where time goes) and blocked_stacks (cpuCycles=0 scheduling event callstacks = why a thread came off CPU, e.g. a fence/wait call). Pass --metric <globalTid> (from thread_scheduling) to attribute one thread and --frame <N> to restrict samples to that frame window; without a metric symbols mix across threads. Use kernel_variance for kernel-duration spread and outlier evidence. Use nccl_distribution to distinguish NCCL event-table evidence from CUDA kernel names that contain nccl. Use nsight_compute_handoff for candidate kernels for separate Nsight Compute inspection.
